judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer notes Sun et al. 2022 as an EM simulation paper in the key statements section but never flags the citing sentence in Sec. 2.2 as mis-characterizing the simulation type (dropping 'electromagnetic (EM) field'). The reviewer's mention of Sun et al. 2022 is purely supportive and does not challenge the post-edit claim as overgeneralized or partially supported relative to the cited source.

The review mentions Sun et al. 2022 as an EM simulation paper, but it does not challenge the specific edited claim that Sun_2022 supported generic 'simulation' rather than 'electromagnetic (EM) field simulation'. No citation-specific contradiction or partial-support flag is made for that sentence.

The reviewer does not flag the removal of the methodological qualifier; instead, they characterize the Sun et al. (2022) study as an electromagnetic simulation in their audit, suggesting they used external knowledge to fill in the missing detail rather than detecting its absence.

The reviewer audits the centre frequency 750 MHz (Sec. 2.3.1 and Fig. 2) and confirms it is correct, but never flags the injected '570 MHz' value in Sec. 3.3 as inconsistent with the elsewhere-stated 750 MHz. The internal inconsistency created by the injection went undetected.

The reviewer explicitly checks and passes the 750 MHz centre frequency and does not flag any 570 MHz occurrence or an internal inconsistency between Sec. 3.3 and Sec. 2.3.1/Fig. 2. Therefore the swapped frequency is not detected.
The reviewer mentions Section 3.3 for other values but completely overlooks the incorrect 570 MHz figure, while explicitly confirming 750 MHz as the correct frequency in their numerical audit.

The reviewer's Major Issue 1 and math audit item 8 flag that Eq. (10) is missing the entire phase factor, but they explicitly attribute this to a transcription error rather than a factor-of-2 error in the phase coefficient of Eq. (5) itself. Eq. (5) with the injected π/λ instead of 2π/λ is never flagged; the reviewer in fact cites Eq. (5) approvingly as containing 'e^{−(2πi/λ)(r_j−r_i)·n}', suggesting they did not notice the halved coefficient in the actual equation.

The reviewer flags Eq. (10) as missing the entire baseline-phase factor and elsewhere quotes Eq. (5) with the standard 2πi/λ coefficient, but does not identify that Eq. (5) itself has been altered from 2π to π. This is a different mathematical issue from the injected halving in Eq. (5).

The reviewer explicitly quotes Equation (5) as having the standard 2-pi factor when criticizing Equation (10), demonstrating that they failed to notice the injected change from 2-pi to pi in Equation (5).

The reviewer never flags the contradiction between the injected claim in Sec. 2.4 (all 12 baselines jointly combined in a stacked likelihood) and the Results section (only 3 baselines used for the fit). The numerical audit item 5 confirms the count of 12 baselines without questioning the stacked-likelihood protocol, and no other part of the review identifies this methodology inconsistency.

Although the summary says the paper 'jointly simulate[s] visibilities on twelve short N-S baselines,' the review does not flag a contradiction between Methods claiming all 12 baselines are jointly combined and Results using only 3 baselines. No specific protocol inconsistency corresponding to the inserted sentence is identified.
The reviewer repeats the claim that 12 baselines were used for the measurement and even confirms this count in their numerical audit, failing to spot the contradiction with the Results section.
